subject: Shared home-office layouts
hook: Office on weekdays, guest room at weekends: does it work?
fb:
A question we get a lot at design consultations: "We need a home office for two, but it's also our only guest room. Can it do both?"

It can, as long as it's planned that way from the start. Keep the desks along one wall so there's clear floor for a bed. Give the office side closed cupboards so laptops and paperwork disappear when someone visits. And leave a wardrobe section or a couple of drawers empty so guests have somewhere to unpack.

Have a question about your own room? Ask in the comments or book a free, no-obligation consultation below.

gbp:
Can a shared home office still work as a guest room? Yes — if it's designed that way from the start.

The key is keeping the floor clear. Desks run along one wall rather than into the room, so there's space for a bed or sofa bed. Closed cupboards and drawers on the office side mean laptops, files and printers can be put away when guests stay. A fitted wardrobe section or a few spare drawers gives visitors somewhere to unpack.
